title: Provisioning runbook: request pipeline, approval lattice, and contingency capacity lanes
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Purpose: Create an operational runbook that standardizes how teams request, approve, and provision Dedicated capacity with explicit throughput guarantees and automated contingency lanes. Scope covers the intake form, automated eligibility checks, approval lattice (fast-path + escalations), capacity runway forecasting, and integration points with autoscaling policies and fleet controls.

Background: We have multiple ad-hoc reservation practices across sales and SRE that cause over-provisioning or missed commitments. This ticket drives a repeatable flow that reduces manual back-and-forth by 50% for standard reservations, and ensures predictable SLAs for committed throughput.

High-level flow we will implement: 
1) Intake: teams submit a standardized Capacity Request form (link to template). Basic validations run (region, model family, expected qps, burst window).
2) Eligibility checks: automated checks against current fleet utilization, reserved headroom, and customer tier. If checks pass, route to the fast-path approval lane.
3) Fast-path approval lane: for small/standard requests (<= X qps, <= 4-week runway) the system issues provisional capacity with a 24-hour SLO for confirmation.
4) Manual approval lattice: for larger or risky requests route to a policy-driven approval queue that includes Product, SRE, and Sales depending on cost and compliance tags. Approvals are recorded and referenced to onboarding docs.
5) Provisioning & handshake: the Dedicated orchestration service provisions the reservation, returns capacity IDs, and schedules a post-provision health check.
6) Contingency lanes / fallbacks: define automatic fallback policies: model-variant degrade (quantized or smaller model), regional failover, or queued requests with guaranteed back-off. Fallbacks must be configurable per customer.
7) Autoscale & fleet controls: connect reservation metadata to autoscaling policies that respect committed throughput windows and burst allowances. Include automatic rollback triggers when provisioning violates SLOs.
8) Forecast & runway: provide a 6-12 week runway forecast for committed capacity, with advisories on when to expand fleet or convert reserved to committed.

Integration points & artifacts:
- Intake template (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/CapacityRequestTemplate
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Capacity+Provisioning+Runbook
- Platform PR for orchestration hooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1347
- Console draft dashboard (forecast & runway): https://console.redwood.ai/dedicated/fleet/forecast-50123

Acceptance criteria (see acceptance_criteria field). Implementation must be instrumented so we can measure time-to-provision and manual-approval reduction.
acceptance_criteria: Standard intake form exists in Drive and is referenced from Confluence.
Automated eligibility checks run on submission and return deterministic thumbs (fast-path or escalation).
Fast-path lane provisions standard reservations within 24 hours end-to-end in >= 80% of cases during pilot.
Manual approval lattice enforces approver matrix and records decisions in audit log.
Provisioned reservations produce capacity IDs and are visible in the Console forecast UI.
Contingency lanes are defined and at least two fallback options (model-variant and regional) are implemented for pilot customers.
Reservation metadata is wired into autoscaling policies so committed throughput windows are honored and do not trigger autoscale thrashing.
Metrics: measure and report manual approval time, provisioning success rate, and runway forecast accuracy in the pilot dashboard.
